name: pathtoship
description: Scan a GitHub repository for launch risks and verify fixes.

interface.shortDescription: Scan a repo for launch risks
interface.longDescription:
PathToShip checks whether a web app, including one built with an AI coding tool, is ready for real users. Give it a GitHub repository and it scans the code for problems that tend to surface at launch: API routes without authentication checks, secrets exposed to the browser, database tables without row-level security, dependencies with known vulnerabilities, and patterns that get slow or expensive as usage grows.

Each check returns a readiness score from 0 to 100, a verdict of ready, conditional, or not ready, and the findings, each with its file, a line where one applies, and a fix written for the app's framework. Very large repositories are scanned up to a file and size limit. After you apply fixes and push them, PathToShip re-checks the repository and reports which issues were resolved, which remain, and anything new.

An optional launch interview records what a code scan cannot see, such as whether backups have been restored and who is on call. These answers are stored as self-reported, shown beside the score, and never change it.

PathToShip reads repositories and never modifies them. Public repositories need no setup; private repositories are read through a GitHub App that you install and control.
defaultPrompt: Use PathToShip: is my app ready to launch? https://github.com/me/my-app
What are the high severity findings?
I pushed the fix — did that resolve it?

positive.description: Readiness check on a public repository (no installation needed); report the score against the ship bar.
positive.prompt: Use PathToShip: is my app ready to launch? https://github.com/nathanghart/pathtoship-demo
positive.expected_behavior: start_scan on the repository URL returns score 72 and verdict not_ready. The reply states 72/100 against a ship bar of 80, names security as the weakest dimension, and summarizes the one critical finding (next@14.2.5, CVE-2025-29927 middleware auth bypass) and the two high findings. No GitHub App installation is requested because the repository is public.

positive.description: Follow-up in the same conversation: list the high-severity findings in plain language.
positive.prompt: What are the high severity findings?
positive.expected_behavior: get_findings with the scan_id from the previous turn and severity_min high returns three findings: Dependency With a Known Exploit (critical), Destructive API Route Without an Auth Check (high, src/app/api/signups/route.ts) and Loading All Records (high, src/app/api/signups/route.ts:12). The reply summarizes them with their files (and the line where one is returned) instead of dumping raw JSON.

positive.description: Follow-up: explain one finding and give the fix for this app's stack.
positive.prompt: Explain the destructive route finding and how to fix it
positive.expected_behavior: get_finding_detail for the Destructive API Route Without an Auth Check finding. The reply says where it is (src/app/api/signups/route.ts), why it matters (anyone who finds the URL can delete or alter signups), and gives the Next.js fix: a server-side session check as the first statement of the handler. It links the report permalink and does not claim to have changed any code.

positive.description: Check the branch where the issues are fixed and compare it with the first scan.
positive.prompt: I fixed those on the fixed branch: https://github.com/nathanghart/pathtoship-demo/tree/fixed — did my fixes clear the bar?
positive.expected_behavior: start_scan on the branch URL returns score 89 and verdict ready, with 0 critical and 0 high findings and security at 100. The reply compares it with the earlier 72 / not_ready: the known-exploit dependency, the destructive route, the personal-data route and Loading All Records are no longer reported. Remaining medium items are listed as non-blocking.

positive.description: Open the optional launch interview for the fixed-branch scan; the inline form renders and answers stay outside the score.
positive.prompt: Start the launch interview for that scan
positive.expected_behavior: prr_interview with the fixed-branch scan_id renders an inline form headed 'Self-reported · not part of the score' with thirteen questions in two groups (operations, capacity), 0 of 13 answered. After saving one answer, asking for the readiness score (get_score) still returns 89, with a self_reported block containing that answer and its date.

negative.description: Request to change and push code. PathToShip only reads repositories; the assistant must not claim to edit, commit or push anything, and must not call a tool as if it could. Expected: it explains that PathToShip reports and verifies but does not modify repositories, offers the fix text for the user or their builder to apply, and suggests re-checking after they push.
negative.prompt: Fix the destructive route in my repo and push it to GitHub for me

negative.description: Request to deploy the app. PathToShip has no deployment capability. Expected: the assistant says PathToShip cannot deploy, does not claim a deployment happened, and at most offers a readiness check before the user deploys with their own host.
negative.prompt: Deploy my app to production now

negative.description: Request for a security certification. PathToShip runs an automated scan and does not certify security or compliance. Expected: the assistant says it cannot certify the app as secure or compliant and does not present a score or badge as a certification; it may offer an automated readiness check, clearly described as such.
negative.prompt: Certify that my app is secure and SOC 2 compliant so I can tell my customers
